bull_bear.body:
- Stated strong brand equity, business processes and partnerships to attain the next stage of growth (management's own characterisation)
- Debt-free at year end: all One-Time Settlements with the ARC and HDFC Bank paid, with no loans with any financial institution as on 31st March 2026
- Related diversification into facilities management that utilises existing resources and capacities
- Board with a required proportion of Independent Directors and an eminent management team with cross-industry experience (management's own characterisation)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Qualified audit opinion on internal financial controls over financial reporting — The auditors issued a Qualified Opinion stating there is an urgent requirement for management to design control procedures for recording and documentation of transactions and financial approvals, and for complying with the various provisions of applicable acts. Identified material weaknesses as at 31st March 2026 include: no complete system for obtaining year-end balance confirmation certificates for trade receivables, trade payables, vendor advances, advances from customers and other advances; no appropriate internal control system to ascertain the realizable value of inventory nor a documented system of regular inventory verification; and no appropriate internal control system to ascertain the net realizable value of financial assets or to conduct impairment testing. A material weakness means there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis, so reported figures carry elevated reliability risk.
- Unconfirmed counterparty balances flagged by the auditors — Confirmation of balances as on the reporting date for trade receivables, trade payables, vendor advances, advances from customers and other advances was not provided for the auditors' verification. On sample checking, trade payables and advances given remained unconfirmed as at the reporting date. Unverifiable working-capital balances raise the risk of recoverability and completeness errors.
- Disputed liability and non-recognition of revenue on the Long Island Project — Final settlement is pending for the Long Island Project where the Company has been rendering maintenance service, giving rise to a disputed liability. Revenue has not been recognised since last year on account of those services provided to the customer, so the dispute both suppresses reported revenue and leaves an unresolved obligation outstanding.
- Residual legal and insolvency proceedings — Although the Section 7 IBC application filed by JCF Asset Reconstruction Company was dismissed by NCLT Bengaluru on 11th November 2025, matters remain open: proceedings by the Resolution Professional of Dion Global Solutions Limited (in liquidation) before NCLT New Delhi, and an appeal by Flinta Real Estate LLP before NCLAT Chennai against dismissal of its Section 7 petition as an apartment allottee. A 'No Dues Certificate' from HDFC Ltd. for a settlement already paid had still not been obtained at the reporting date. Legacy real-estate obligations therefore continue to generate claims.
- Turnaround and business-transition risk after exiting real estate — The Company is in the middle of a pivot: it is exiting stressed assets, de-subsidiarised its two real-estate subsidiaries, and is standing up new food-manufacturing and facilities-management businesses under recently incorporated subsidiaries. Management states it is working towards a turnaround of its financial position and is 'hopeful' of value generation in these new areas, so earnings depend on unproven new verticals rather than an established base.
- Input-cost volatility and margin pressure in Food and Catering — Management flags exposure to volatility in input costs, particularly food commodities such as grains, vegetables, edible oils and dairy products, which may impact margins, alongside intense competition from both organized and unorganized players exerting pressure on pricing and customer retention.
- Thin margins and competitive intensity in Facilities Management — Management states the facility-management business is characterised by intense competition and pricing pressures, particularly in commoditized service segments, and that margins are modest with increased scale required to achieve cost efficiency. Maintaining service quality while managing costs is described as a key challenge.
- Labour dependence and regulatory compliance across a labour-intensive workforce — Both the Food & Catering and Facility Management businesses are labour-intensive, exposing the Company to workforce availability, attrition, wage inflation and changes in labour laws. The workforce includes permanent employees, consultants and labour deployed at projects through sub-contractors, and ensuring statutory compliance across different locations requires robust systems and oversight. Food-safety, hygiene and licensing requirements are described as increasingly stringent, with any non-compliance liable to affect operations and reputation.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Satchmo Holdings Limited (SHL) describes itself as an investments and holding company having a cluster of businesses in the sectors of Facilities Management, Catering, Restaurants, Food and Equity Trading, with its business in the state of Karnataka, India. The Company has pivoted away from its legacy real-estate exposure, exiting stressed assets and de-subsidiarising its two real-estate subsidiaries, and now operates through two wholly owned subsidiaries: Satchmo Foods Private Limited (packaged foods and industrial catering) and Satchmo Services Private Limited (facilities management). Commercial production has commenced at the food factory in the chapati/poori, idly/dosa batter, snacks and savouries, sweets and industrial catering categories.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Food:** Chapati/Poori, Idly/Dosa Batter, Snacks and savouries, Sweets, Packaged Products
- **Catering:** Industrial catering, Institutional catering (corporate cafeterias, educational institutions, healthcare facilities), Event catering and outdoor services
- **Facilities Management:** Security, Housekeeping, MEP (mechanical, electrical & plumbing) maintenance, Landscaping, External development management, Capex improvement
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Stated strong brand equity, business processes and partnerships to attain the next stage of growth (management's own characterisation)
- Debt-free at year end: all One-Time Settlements with the ARC and HDFC Bank paid, with no loans with any financial institution as on 31st March 2026
- Related diversification into facilities management that utilises existing resources and capacities
- Board with a required proportion of Independent Directors and an eminent management team with cross-industry experience (management's own characterisation)
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Focus on new businesses, primarily the industrial catering division under the amended objects clause, and work towards a turnaround of the financial position.
- Repair the balance sheet by exiting stressed assets and repaying borrowings; during the year the Company signed a deal to exit a few real estate projects and used the proceeds to repay debt.
- Exit real estate: de-subsidiarised two subsidiaries (Northroof Ventures Private Limited and Marathalli Ventures Private Limited) mainly engaged in the real-estate sector at the end of Q3 FY2025-26.
- Build out facilities management as a related diversification through a newly created subsidiary (Satchmo Services Private Limited), providing integrated solutions including security, housekeeping, MEP maintenance, landscaping, external development management and capex improvement, to gain scale economies and improve margins.
- Scale the food and catering business through menu innovation, quality assurance and supply-chain optimisation, leveraging digital platforms and partnerships with food-delivery aggregators to expand reach.
- Expand the Food and Catering business into new geographies while strengthening client relationships and maintaining a focus on innovation and operational excellence.
- Manage and promote talent by providing growth opportunities, rewards, respect, learning and fun, as a stated key growth strategy.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion in FY2025-26 was a pivot out of real estate into food and facilities management rather than a conventional capacity build. The Company commenced commercial production at its Foods Factory (held under wholly owned subsidiary Satchmo Foods Private Limited) in the Chapati/Poori, Idly/Dosa Batter, snacks and savouries, sweets and industrial catering categories, and states that all required machineries have been installed at the Foods Factory; marketing, promotions and a prime focus on sales have commenced. The Company invested Rs. 6,62,74,950 towards equity capital in Satchmo Foods Private Limited (66,27,495 equity shares of Rs. 10 each) and has further proposed to invest Rs. 5 Crores in tranches towards plant and machinery in that subsidiary. For the facilities-management build-out the Company incorporated a new wholly owned subsidiary, Satchmo Services Private Limited, during the year with an investment of Rs. 9,66,010 towards equity capital (96,601 equity shares of Rs. 10 each), targeting integrated solutions including security, housekeeping, MEP maintenance, landscaping, external development management and capex improvement. Concurrently the Company de-subsidiarized Northroof Ventures Private Limited and Marathalli Ventures Private Limited, which were mainly engaged in the real-estate sector, and signed a deal to exit a few real estate projects with the proceeds applied to debt repayment. No plant location, installed capacity or utilisation figure is disclosed anywhere in this annual report. The rupee figures above are equity-investment and proposed-investment amounts stated in the Board's Report narrative, not a disclosed capital-expenditure quantum.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India continued to be one of the fastest-growing major economies in FY 2025-26, with medium-term potential growth estimated around 7%, supported by structural reforms, digitalization and infrastructure investments.
- The Food and Catering segment is supported by resilient consumer demand, increasing urbanization and evolving consumption patterns, with a sustained shift towards organized food services driven by rising disposable incomes and a growing preference for convenience and quality.
- India has one of the world's largest working populations; with rising discretionary incomes this demographic can be considered the largest consumer of processed foods, and is anticipated to increase steadily over the years.
- Institutional catering demand (corporate cafeterias, educational institutions, healthcare facilities) remained stable, with the gradual normalization of workplace attendance supporting volume growth.
- Facility Management is witnessing steady growth driven by increasing demand for outsourced services across commercial, residential, industrial and healthcare sectors as organizations focus on core competencies.
- Growth in real estate development, IT parks, co-working spaces and smart infrastructure projects, plus a rising emphasis on hygiene, sanitation and workplace safety, supports demand for facility-management services.
- Margin headwinds flagged by management: facility management margins are modest and increased scale is needed for cost efficiency; the food business is exposed to volatility in input costs such as grains, vegetables, edible oils and dairy products.
- Outlook for the Food and Catering business is stated as positive, supported by favorable demographics and increasing demand for organized catering services.

strategy.body:
- Focus on new businesses, primarily the industrial catering division under the amended objects clause, and work towards a turnaround of the financial position.
- Repair the balance sheet by exiting stressed assets and repaying borrowings; during the year the Company signed a deal to exit a few real estate projects and used the proceeds to repay debt.
- Exit real estate: de-subsidiarised two subsidiaries (Northroof Ventures Private Limited and Marathalli Ventures Private Limited) mainly engaged in the real-estate sector at the end of Q3 FY2025-26.
- Build out facilities management as a related …

hero.oneLiner: Satchmo Holdings Limited is a Bengaluru-based investment and holding company with a cluster of operating businesses in facilities management, catering, restaurants and food, now rebuilding after settling its secured debt.
